children.translated_text: had become full of holes, had become thin—the community of monks. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who are knowers and questioners, ask. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, asked the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'What, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the cause, what is the condition, that now the monks have become few? That the community of monks has reached decline, has become full of holes, has become thin?' He reported this matter to the Blessed One in detail.

body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In the absence of dispassion, monks commit <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (offenses requiring formal meeting of the saṅgha) offenses. They, having become remorseful, reflect: 'How can we now, being guilty of offenses, full of remorse, full of agitation, having duties to perform, makers of breaks, makers of patches, makers of stains, not having risen from the root of the offense, accept the acts of greeting, salutation, rising, <s>añjali</s> (palms joined in respect), and proper conduct from monks who are in good standing? And from faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, enjoy the first seat, the first water, and the first almsfood? For the sake of short-lived happiness, we will incur long-lasting suffering, wandering among hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts. Let us rather renounce the training and return to the lower state.' Thus they renounce the training and return to the lower state. And they deceive people who desire ordination, saying: 'Sirs, the holy life is hard to practice; enough with ordination.' Because of those among them who had not gone forth

children.text: saṃghaṃ saṃnipātya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / śrutaṃ mayā bhikṣavaḥ saṃghāvaśeṣām āpattim āpannā vipratisārajātāḥ śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāya hānāyāvṛttā iti / tasmād yuṣmābhiḥ śāsanasthitaye teṣāṃ cānukampayā saṃghāvaśeṣām āpattim āpannānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ parivāso deyo mūlāpakarṣo mānāpyaṃ mūlamānāpyaṃ mūlāpakarṣamānāpyam āvarhitavyaś ca /
children.translated_text: monks, and having seated himself on a seat prepared before the community of monks, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'I have heard, monks, that those who have committed <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses, having become remorseful, have renounced the training and returned to the lower state. Therefore, for the stability of the teaching and out of compassion for them, you should give <s>parivāsa</s> (probation) to monks who have committed <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses, <s>mūlāpakarṣa</s> (sending back to the beginning), <s>mānāpya</s> (penance), <s>mūlamānāpya</s> (penance from the root), <s>mūlāpakarṣamānāpya</s> (penance with sending back to the beginning), and they should be rehabilitated.'

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One had this thought: 'Let me extend a helping hand to the monks who have committed <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses, this being an act of assistance.' Having understood this, he convened the

body.text: evaṃ ca punar deyaḥ / śayanāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvā gaṇḍīm ākoṭya pṛṣṭavācikayā bhikṣūn samanuyujya sarvasaṃghe saṃniṣaṇṇe saṃnipatite apaścimakena bhikṣuṇā parivāso deyaś caturvargamaṇḍalakena / saṃghāvaśeṣakeṇa bhikṣuṇā yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā vṛddhānte utkuṭukena sthitvāñjaliṃ pragṛhya parivāso yācitavyaḥ / evaṃ ca punar yācitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And furthermore, it should be given thus: having arranged the seats, having struck the <s>gaṇḍī</s> (wooden gong), having assembled the monks by a proclamation from behind, when the entire <s>saṅgha</s> has sat down and assembled, <s>parivāsa</s> (probation) should be given by the last monk, with a quorum of four. The monk who has committed a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense, having performed the proper respect according to seniority, standing at the end of the senior monks in a squatting position with palms joined, should request <s>parivāsa</s>. And it should be requested thus:'

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / aham evaṃnāmā bhikṣuḥ saṃbahulāḥ saṃghāvaśeṣā āpattīr āpannaḥ saṃcintyaśukravisṛṣṭisamutthitām ardhamāsapraticchannām* / so 'ham evaṃnāmā bhikṣus tāsāṃ saṃbahulānāṃ saṃghāvaśeṣāṇāṃ āpattīnāṃ saṃcintyaśukravisṛṣṭisamutthitām ardhamāsapraticchannāṃ saṃghād ardhamāsaṃ parivāsaṃ yāce / dadātu me bhadantaḥ saṃgho mamaivaṃnāmno bhikṣor āsāṃ saṃbahulānāṃ saṃghāvaśeṣāṇāṃ āpattīnāṃ saṃcintyaśukravisṛṣṭisamutthitānām ardhamāsapraticchannānām ardhamāsaṃ parivāsam anukaṃpayānukaṃpām upādāya / evaṃ dvir api trir api / tataḥ paścād ekena bhikṣuṇā jñaptiṃ kṛtvā karma kartavyam* /
body.translated_text: 'Let the noble <s>saṅgha</s> hear me. I, the monk named so-and-so, have committed numerous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, concealed for half a month. I, the monk named so-and-so, request from the <s>saṅgha</s> a half-month <s>parivāsa</s> (probation) for those numerous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, concealed for half a month. May the noble <s>saṅgha</s> grant me, the monk named so-and-so, a half-month <s>parivāsa</s> for those numerous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from intentional emission of semen, concealed for half a month, out of compassion, having undertaken compassion.' Thus a second and third time. Then afterwards, one monk, having made the motion (<s>jñapti</s>), should perform the formal act (<s>karma</s>).

children.translated_text: -merous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from the intentional emission of semen, a <s>parivāsa</s> of a half-month. If the venerable ones approve granting to this <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, for these numerous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from the intentional emission of semen, concealed for a half-month, a <s>parivāsa</s> of a half-month — let them be silent. Those who do not approve — let them speak. This is the first proclamation of the formal act (<s>karmavācanā</s>) to be recited. The <s>Saṃgha</s> has granted to this <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, for these numerous <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses arising from the intentional emission of semen, concealed for a half-month, a <s>parivāsa</s> of a half-month. It has been approved and consented to by the <s>Saṃgha</s>, since they are silent — thus I hold it. The Blessed One said: 'A <s>parivāsa</s> should be granted — a root <s>parivāsa</s> (<s>mūlaparivāsa</s>)' — and so on in detail.

children.translated_text: Nor on an equal seat. If they do sit, they should take a lower seat. They should not walk on the walkway simultaneously [with regular monks]. Nor in front [of them]. If they walk on the walkway, [they should walk] yielding a step. They should not visit <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> households [for alms]. If they do visit, [they should go] behind, in the manner of ascetics. They should not dwell under the same roof [as regular monks]. They should not ordain (<s>pravrajya</s>). They should not confer full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>). They should not give guidance (<s>niśraya</s>). They should not appoint a novice (<s>śramaṇoddeśin</s>). They should not perform formal acts (<s>karma</s>). They should not be designated as performers of formal acts. They should not instruct <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>s (nuns). They should not be designated as instructors of <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>s. They should not instruct <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>s [even] by prior designation. They should not reprove a <s>bhikṣu</s>.

children.text: ) smārayitavyaḥ śīlavipattyā dṛṣṭivipattyā ācāravipattyā ājīvavipattyā / nānenāvavādaḥ sthāpayitavyaḥ / na poṣadho na pravāraṇā na jñaptir na jñaptidvitīyaṃ na jñapticaturthaṃ karma / kālyam evotthāya dvāraṃ bhoktavyam* / dīpasthālaka udvartavyaḥ / vihāraḥ sektavyaḥ / saṃmārṣṭavyaḥ / sukumārī gomayakārṣī anupradātavyā / prasrāvoccārakuṭī dhāvayitavyā / mṛttikā upasthāpayitavyā pātrāṇi pānīyaṃ śītalaṃ vā kālānurūpataḥ / praṇāḍikāmukhāni dhāvayitavyāni / kālaṃ jñātvāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvā dhūpakaṭacchūke dhūpaś copasthāpayitavaḥ / sacet pratibalo bhavati śāstur guṇasaṃkīrtanaṃ kartuṃ svayam eva kartavyam* / noced bhāṣaṇakaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ upānvāhāraṃ pratyavekṣyopānvāhṛtaṃ cec charaṇapṛṣṭham abhiruhya gaṇḍīr (
children.translated_text: ) he should be admonished for transgression of moral conduct, transgression of views, transgression of behavior, and transgression of livelihood. He should not be given formal instruction (<s>avavāda</s>). Neither <s>poṣadha</s> (confession ceremony), nor <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony), nor <s>jñapti</s> (motion), nor <s>jñaptidvitīya</s> (motion with one proclamation), nor <s>jñapticaturtha</s> (motion with three proclamations) <s>karma</s> (ecclesiastical act) [should be performed by him]. He should rise early and eat at the door. The lamp-stand should be polished. The <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) should be sprinkled and swept. Soft cow-dung plaster should be applied. The latrines should be washed. Clay should be set out; bowls, drinking water, or cold [water] according to the season. The mouths of the drains should be washed. Having noted the time and having arranged the seats, incense and the incense-ladle should be set up. If he is able to proclaim the virtues of the Teacher, he should do it himself. If not, the speaker should be asked. Having examined the food offering, if it has been brought, climbing up on the back of the steps, the gong (

And it should be taken up thus: having made proper obeisance, standing in a squatting position, with <s>añjali</s> (palms joined), the following should be said: 'May the venerable one attend! I, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, have committed such-and-such a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense, concealed for such-and-such a period. The <s>Saṃgha</s> has given me a <s>parivāsa</s> for such-and-such a period. I, while being on <s>parivāsa</s>, heard that <s>bhikṣu</s>s are coming — quarrel-makers, dispute-makers, conflict-makers, contention-makers, litigants — who would reprove me and remind me [of my offense], whether shamelessly or contentiously. That <s>parivāsa</s> observance was relinquished by me in the presence of a <s>bhikṣu</s>. I, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, take up that <s>parivāsa</s> again in the presence of the venerable one. I have performed this much time; this much remains to be performed. May the venerable one regard me as one on <s>parivāsa</s>.'

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Upāli</s> asks the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One): 'Reverend Sir, inasmuch as by <s>pārivāsikas</s> (those on probation) and <s>mānāpyacārikas</s> (those undergoing penance)

body.text: yathā parivāsa evaṃ mūlaparivāso mūlāpakarṣo mānāpyaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: As [is the procedure] for the <s>parivāsa</s>, so too for the <s>mūlaparivāsa</s> (root probation), the <s>mūlāpakarṣa</s> (drawing back to the root), and the <s>mānāpya</s> (penance).

body.text: pārivāsikavastu samāptam* //
body.translated_text: The <s>Pārivāsikavastu</s> (Section on Probation) is completed.
